candidates.change_summary: Swap the order of incrementing totalSupply and crediting the recipient balance inside _mint, so a reentrant observer reading totalSupply via an ERC-677 hook before the balance update sees a different value.
Assign `mapSynth_LPBalance[msg.sender]` to `lpUnits + mapSynth_LPBalance[msg.sender]` instead of the original `mapSynth_LPBalance[msg.sender] += lpUnits` by rewriting to an explicit addition.
Remove the `mapSynth_LPBalance[msg.sender] += lpUnits` line so that LP balance is never incremented.
Replace `_getAddedLPAmount(msg.sender)` with `_getAddedLPAmount(member)` so LP units are calculated from the recipient instead of the caller pool.

Remove the `onlyPool` modifier from `mintSynth` by rewriting the modifier body to always return true, making `mintSynth` callable by any account, which changes `mapSynth_LPBalance` values due to unrestricted access.
Weaken the onlyPool modifier guard to accept any caller instead of requiring a curated pool.
Credit the caller's LP balance with the passed synthetic amount instead of the measured newly added LP collateral amount.
Delete the update to the caller's synthetic LP debt so it no longer increases.
Delete the update to the caller's synthetic LP balance so it no longer increases.
Insert a sync of the measured added LP amount into the caller's synthetic LP balance before the debt update.
Delete the mapSynth_LPDebt update, so mintSynth no longer records the caller's synth debt balance.
Delete the mapSynth_LPBalance update, so mintSynth records debt but not the LP collateral balance used by burnSynth.
Delete the onlyPool modifier, allowing any caller to invoke mintSynth and mutate the debt mapping without being a curated pool.
Delete the isCuratedPool require in the onlyPool modifier, so any caller passes the pool guard.
Replace the transfer statement body with an empty block so it returns true without moving any tokens.
Replace the returned boolean in the transfer function with a false literal.
Replace the call to _approve with an always-false return, so approve still completes without reverting but returns false instead of true.
Replace the call to _approve with an always-true return, so approve skips updating allowances and returns true without performing the approval side effect.
Replace the allowance update with a no-op statement, leaving allowance unchanged but still returning true.
Return false instead of true after successfully updating the allowance.
Replace the _approve call's amount argument with a computed value that omits the subtraction, so the new allowance is currentAllowance instead of currentAllowance - subtractedValue.
Replace the require condition with a check that currentAllowance is greater than subtractedValue, reverting on the equality case.
Replace the returned boolean true with false.
Replace the subtracted allowance calculation with addition, increasing the allowance instead of decreasing it.
Change the balance precondition from `currentAllowance >= subtractedValue` to `currentAllowance != subtractedValue`, so a spender cannot decrease an allowance by exactly the current allowance.
Change the subtraction to addition in the new allowance calculation, so decreaseAllowance increases the allowance instead of decreasing it.
Return false instead of true on a successful decreaseAllowance call.
Remove the require precondition so decreaseAllowance no longer reverts when subtractedValue exceeds the current allowance; underflow reverts instead.
Change the precondition to reject zero subtractedValue instead of insufficient allowance, altering which inputs revert.
Replace the early _transfer call with an empty statement, leaving transferFrom to return true without moving tokens.
Weaken the allowance check so transferFrom succeeds even when the current allowance is less than the requested amount.
Change the branch condition so allowance bookkeeping is skipped whenever the allowance is nonzero.
Read the owner’s allowance for the caller twice, using msg.sender as the spender for the subtraction amount.
Approve the zero address on behalf of the sender, causing _approve’s spender guard to revert for non-max allowances.
Move the _transfer call from before the allowance branch to immediately before the return, changing reentrancy-visible state during allowance updates.
Insert an unconditional allowance reset after the branch, overwriting the sender’s allowance to the caller before returning.
Delete the early _transfer call so transferFrom no longer moves tokens before updating allowance.
